prompt:
Solve the running-time recurrence below.

```formula essential
T(n) = T(n/2) + T(n/4) + n
where
T: the total running time
n: the input size
In words: A half-size child and a quarter-size child are followed by linear outside work.
```

Assume bounded positive base-case costs and the usual integer rounding of fractional child sizes.

options.explanation: This would need each level to do about n work. Here the subproblem sizes add up to only 3/4 of the parent's size, so level totals shrink.
This treats the recurrence as three half-size children. The actual two children are a half and a quarter, so their total size is smaller.
Correct. The balancing exponent is below one, and the outside-work correction supplies the remaining power, leaving linear total growth.
The root alone does n work, so T(n) is at least n.

workedExample: Half-size and quarter-size children together contain three quarters of the parent’s size. Their combined linear outside work therefore shrinks geometrically down the tree. The root already costs linear work and the whole tree adds only a constant multiple, giving Θ(n) in original input size n. Unequal children do not require pretending they are equal.
